title: Corporate-actions API release stalled mid-rollout
telemetry: Supplied sanitized GKE console observations (Deployment, ReplicaSet, Pod, Service endpoint and PodDisruptionBudget status and Kubernetes events), k8s_pod and k8s_container log entries, a Cloud Monitoring request chart, and owner-supplied release-pipeline, change and cluster-operation records. owner: Folasade, Corporate Actions on-call, owns the investigation; Caspian, the corp-actions-api application and release owner, owns its code, Deployment manifest, rollout strategy, PodDisruptionBudget and any rollback or fix-forward; Henrike, the GKE platform owner, owns cluster corpactions-gke, its node provisioning and maintenance. ITO coordinates the existing TLC and change approvals.
task: Folasade has asked you to investigate why the release 5.2.0 rollout of Deployment corp-actions-api in cluster corpactions-gke, namespace corp-actions, project synthetic-corpactions-prod, us-east1 has not completed. Review the supplied console observations for 2026-10-16 10:20-10:58 UTC and return an evidence-grounded technical update for the existing TLC: rollout state, healthy serving capacity, the mechanism the records support, remaining unknowns, and the recovery options with the owner who must approve them. No change is authorized.

sources.claim: maxSurge and maxUnavailable default to 25%; a percentage resolves to an absolute number by rounding up for maxSurge and down for maxUnavailable, so 3 replicas allow 1 surge Pod and 0 unavailable. progressDeadlineSeconds defaults to 600; when exceeded the Deployment reports type Progressing, status False, reason ProgressDeadlineExceeded, and Kubernetes takes no other action. Progress means creating or scaling ReplicaSets or new Pods becoming ready or available; with minReadySeconds 0 a Pod is available once ready. Status counts and the condition time are authored fixture values; no condition message text is used.

A Pod whose readiness probe fails is marked unready and receives no traffic through Services; an HTTP probe succeeds only for status codes from 200 up to but not including 400. The kubelet event wording and its count field are fixture observations and are not graded.

Workload resources such as Deployment are not limited by PodDisruptionBudgets when doing rolling upgrades, although Pods unavailable during a rolling upgrade count against the budget; deleting Pods bypasses a PDB. Tools that respect PDBs use the Eviction API, and a drain blocks while an eviction would breach the budget. The PDB status values are authored observations.

Required pod anti-affinity is a hard scheduling filter: a Pod is not placed in a topology domain, named by the topologyKey node label such as a zone, that already runs a matching Pod; preferred anti-affinity only scores nodes. An optional admission controller can restrict required anti-affinity to kubernetes.io/hostname; the fixture's template and FailedScheduling events are supplied observations, and the scheduler message wording is not graded.

Autopilot supports pod affinity and anti-affinity with topologyKey topology.kubernetes.io/zone or kubernetes.io/hostname, and new Autopilot clusters are regional. The page does not say which zones an Autopilot cluster may use; the three node zones, the absent scale-up and the Pending state are supplied observations, not inferences from this page.

Autopilot node upgrades drain nodes by evicting Pods and respect a PodDisruptionBudget for one hour; maintenance windows and exclusions control timing and are honored if possible. The page does not say what happens after that hour, so the case relies only on the PDB being a latent risk to a future drain.

a.conclusion: Revision 8 (5.2.0) created one surge Pod, which was scheduled and is Running without restarts but has failed every readiness probe with HTTP 503 since 10:31:24; its log reports reference schema 41 required and 40 found. With maxUnavailable resolving to 0, the controller keeps all three 5.1.3 Pods until a new Pod is available, so the rollout stalled and reported ProgressDeadlineExceeded at 10:41:02 while 5.1.3 serves all traffic at baseline 5xx with 3 of 3 desired Pods ready. The PodDisruptionBudget does not limit rolling updates, the templates carry no placement constraint and no node operation ran, so none of them is the cause. Why production is at schema 40 is unknown.

With maxUnavailable resolving to 0, the controller will not remove a 5.1.3 Pod until a new Pod is available, so the rollout deadlocks and reported ProgressDeadlineExceeded at 10:41:02. Revision 7 last rolled out at 2 replicas, when a free zone existed; replicas became 3 on 2026-10-13. The 5.2.0 container never ran, so the image is shown neither faulty nor healthy in production. Healthy capacity is 3 of 3 desired Pods on 5.1.3 at baseline 5xx; the PodDisruptionBudget does not limit rolling updates and no node operation ran.
